text:
prod-incident-bot: Pager duty notified: GPU capacity exhaustion detected in aws-us-gov-west-1. Autoscaler is not provisioning new instances, queue growth observed for hosted-api and dedicated customers. Severity: P1. Paging on-call.
Amanda: on it. linking Zoom. starting simple triage - is this quota or failed provisioning?
Raj: seeing 429s from provisioning service and 'QuotaExceeded' from AWS Service Quotas API.
Sofia: confirmed spike in pending-requests metric on routing: queue length +6x in last 10m, tail latency up to 2.3s, 5% 5xxs.
Amanda: thanks. priority: 1) confirm quota hit 2) divert traffic/fallback 3) engage cloud support if needed.
Raj: ran quick check: `aws service-quotas get-service-quota --service-code ec2 --quota-code L-XXXXX --region us-gov-west-1` -> returns 403 QuotaExceeded. snippet:```json
{
  \"Quota\": {
    \"QuotaName\": \"Running On-Demand instances\",
    \"Value\": 0,
    \"Unit\": \"instances\"
  }
}```
Sofia: that matches autoscaler logs: `scaleup_attempt failed: quota_exceeded` and then `no capacity available`.
Tomas: customer impact matrix: hosted-api (public) degraded; Dedicated customers on us-gov-west-1 seeing queued requests; Private deployments unaffected. Noting 3 ongoing jobs in high-priority queue belong to two enterprise customers.
Amanda: putting temporary mitigation in place: 1) enable regional fallback -> route new requests to aws-us-east-2 for non-sensitive tenants, 2) restrict large-batch jobs (sqs throttle for heavy model inference), 3) lower concurrency per VM to reduce immediate queue pressure.
Sofia: initiating routing change now: `routeset apply --region-fallback us-east-2 --match-tag non-sensitive` -> in progress.
ops-bot: Routing change deployed to edge cluster 3/4 nodes. Observability gives a 30s window to verify.
Raj: quick workaround for Dedicated customers: create emergency preemptible pool in us-gov-west-1 using remaining soft quota? AWS reports "soft-limit reached" but there are one-off spare slots on some AZs — manual claim might work. I'm opening an allocation claim now.
Amanda: please coordinate with sales/CS for customer comms if we divert any committed capacity. Tomas, take point on comms.
Tomas: writing a short note for affected customers: "We're seeing regional GPU provisioning delays in us-gov-west-1 causing queued inference requests. We're routing non-sensitive traffic to us-east-2 and working with AWS support to restore capacity. No data plane changes to your workloads. ETA 1-2 hours for full recovery."
Sofia: metrics after routing change: queue length down ~40% for public endpoints, errors trending down. Dedicated queue still at +2x.
Raj: AWS support case opened: case# 123456789 — elevated to urgent. Support says quota backend is stuck and engineering is investigating internal quota propagation for gov regions. They proposed manual quota bump which requires account verification; pushing for immediate temp bump.
Amanda: while we wait for support, enable model fallback to smaller quantized variants for Dedicated jobs so they use less GPU memory per instance. Sofia handle rollout.
Sofia: rolling model-fallback canary to 10% of dedicated traffic now. Command:```bash
redwood ctl rollout --model vip-gpt-67b --fallback vip-gpt-67b-q4_0 --percent 10 --scope dedicated/us-gov-west-1
```
ops-bot: Canary started. Trace-id: trace-0a1b2c.
Raj: manual allocation claim succeeded in AZ-a for 2 x p4d-equivalents but they will be preemptible and short-lived. Adding them to warm pool; should relieve Dedicated queue for ~30-50 minutes.
Amanda: good. monitor customer jobs. If any committed SLA affected we must notify CS and Sales. Tomas please update every 30m.
Tomas: posted to #customer-success: short update and asked for any impacted customer lists.
Sofia: logs show dropped requests when queue > 1200, we've configured backpressure at 900 now to fail fast and surface retries. Added retry-after header to client responses.
Amanda: next steps: 1) wait for AWS manual quota bump, 2) gradually shift more non-sensitive traffic to us-east-2, 3) maintain model fallbacks for Dedicated until stable.
Raj: AWS just updated case: manual bump approved for 10 GPUs in us-gov-west-1, ETA ~22 minutes to propagate.
ops-bot: automated runbook suggests also checking IAM service-linked role for service-quotas. Raj please verify.
Raj: verified service-linked role exists and active. Noting quota propagation is the blocker.
Tomas: customer-impact summary for Slack header: "P1: Regional GPU quota propagation failure in aws-us-gov-west-1. Partial recovery via routing & manual allocation. Some Dedicated customers saw queued requests and elevated latencies. AWS manual quota bump inbound."
Amanda: handoff: I'm staying on this for another 20m then handing off to Raj for stabilization. If AWS bump completes, Raj to monitor and then close. Tomas to keep customer comms. Sofia to revert canary once Dedicated queue normalizes.
Raj: ack. taking on-call. will post status updates every 15m or on major changes.
prod-incident-bot: Incident thread created. Incident ID: INC-2026-1758881111.
Amanda: thanks team. finishing notes in runbook before handoff.
Tomas: update posted to customers; one enterprise replied asking for ETA on committed capacity — I flagged to Sales.
Raj: last checked at 1758881375: AWS bump propagated, new capacity visible, autoscaler success logs: `scaleup_success count=4`. Dedicated queue trending down. Leaving follow-up tasks in ticket.
Amanda: closing pager handoff. leaving postmortem TODO (assign: Amanda, Raj, Sofia, Tomas).
Sofia: adding runbook changes: add gov-region propagation checks and faster pre-claim path.
prod-incident-bot: Status changed to monitoring.
